title: ZZWF07 five-round shifted related-key differential-linear property

target.description: Five nonlinear layers in rounds 2–6, ending at equivalent-key state x6W after SB6, SR6, ARK(w6) and before MC6. Start condition is specified at x1M before ARK(k1); this is not the first-five-round/first-key-relation experiment.

setting.key_relation: Second master-key XOR pattern Table3: active a at byte0 of word0 and word2; other master bytes zero. Nonzero a chosen, dependent b/c generated by the actual key schedule.
setting.key_population: General secret-key pair with the specified master-key XOR relation; no weak-key class is selected.
setting.plaintext_model: Pairs conditioned on Delta x1M=((0,0,0,0),(0,0,0,0),(a,0,0,0),(a,0,0,0)); subsequent rounds 2–6 form the shifted construction.
assumptions: The exact11/5440 bias is a count over uniformly weighted compatible intermediate tuples, not a proof that every fixed related AES key pair induces that distribution. After SR and equivalent-key addition the signed bias is multiplied by (-1)^{lambda dot (Delta w[13] XOR Delta w[10])}; its absolute model bias is unchanged.

property.statement: For any nonzero 8-bit lambda, the source Eq.10 parity lambda dot(Delta x6W[13] XOR Delta x6W[10])=0 has model absolute bias approximately 2^-9; the analogous uniform-compatible-tuple calculation is 8389632/(2^24-2^16)-1/2=11/5440. A fixed equivalent-key parity can reverse its sign.
property.quantifier: All 255 nonzero 8-bit masks under the source shifted related-key construction and local uniformly weighted intermediate-tuple model; not a proved fixed-key distribution theorem.
property.scope: Five-round segment 2–6 with the second master-key XOR pattern; the entering round1 condition is a conditioning requirement, not supplied for free by arbitrary plaintext pairs.

parameters.name: absolute_model_bias
parameters.meaning: Exact local uniform-tuple count; not correlation or whole-attack success.

validation.description: Eq.10 and Table3 read; finite S-box calculation verified all 255 masks, 8160 combined schedule assignments matched Tables 2/3, and linear-map key-offset checks verified the sign caveat. The whole five-round distribution and attack are not reproduced.

time.note: Supporting mathematical intermediate-state property, not a complete key-recovery resource.

success.description: A deterministic equality or a local parity-model bias is not an end-to-end key-recovery success probability.

evidence.locator: PDF8/printed80 Section6 Table3 and Eq.10; PDF6–7/printed78–79 Section4 analogous construction.
evidence.interpretation: Exact primary model and round boundaries checked; supporting property separated from key-recovery budgets.

limitations: Complete 13-page independent primary read and bounded forward-primary review on 2026-10-27. Finite S-box tuple, key-schedule, linear-map and source-exponent checks do not execute or reproduce the whole statistical recovery attack.

The exact11/5440 bias is a count over uniformly weighted compatible intermediate tuples, not a proof that every fixed related AES key pair induces that distribution. After SR and equivalent-key addition the signed bias is multiplied by (-1)^{lambda dot (Delta w[13] XOR Delta w[10])}; its absolute model bias is unchanged.
